title: Catching up
goal: Catch up with a friend you haven't seen for a while: say what you did at the weekend, ask 'have you ever…?', tell them what's happened since you last met, and say how long ago or since when.
intro:
**किती दिवसांनी!** 'It's been ages!' — and then the questions come: **काय म्हणतोस? सध्या काय चाललंय? मध्यंतरी काय काय झालं?** This unit is about that conversation: the trip you took, the trek you finally did, the new job, the friend who's moved abroad, the baby on the way.

To tell it well you need to place things in time. Marathi has a plain past (गेलो), a **perfect** for things that still matter now (गेलोय 'I've gone / I've been'), and a **past perfect** (गेलो होतो) that Marathi uses for a finished outing where English just says 'I went'. You'll also learn the **past continuous** (मी जेवत होतो 'I was eating') for what you were in the middle of, and the time words **-पासून** 'since / for', **-पूर्वी** 'ago' and **-नी** 'after'.

grammar.title: Past, perfect and 'had': गेलो, गेलोय, गेलो होतो
grammar.body:
Marathi has three ways to talk about something that's done, and they don't line up exactly with English.

**1. Plain past** (Unit 16): मी गेलो, तिने पाहिलं. The everyday past, and often what English says with 'have': मी जेवलो 'I've eaten'.

**2. Present perfect** = past form + आहे, which in speech fuses into one word:
मी आलो आहे → **आलोय** (m) · आले आहे → **आलेय** (f)
तू आला आहेस → **आलायस** · आली आहेस → **आलीयस**
तो **आलाय** · ती **आलीय** · ते **आलंय** · ते (pl) **आलेत**
Transitive verbs keep the ergative agreement with the object: मी हा चित्रपट **पाहिलाय**, तिने जेवण **केलंय**.
Use it when the result **still matters now** (तो आलाय 'he's here', माझं वजन वाढलंय 'I've put on weight') and for **experience** with **कधी** 'ever': तू कधी गोव्याला **गेलायस** का? 'have you ever been to Goa?'. 'Never' is just **कधीच** + the plain past negative: मी कधीच गोव्याला **गेलो नाही**.

**3. Past perfect** = past form + **होतो / होती / होतं…**: मी गेलो **होतो**. Besides English 'had gone', Marathi uses it for a **trip or event that is over** — you went and came back: गेल्या वीकेंडला मी लोणावळ्याला **गेलो होतो**. Plain मी लोणावळ्याला गेलो sounds as if you set off and are still there.

**The trap:** don't answer 'have you ever…?' with the perfect in the negative (✗ मी कधीच गेलोय नाही). Say **कधीच गेलो नाही**, or for 'not yet', **अजून गेलो नाही**.

examples.en: Have you ever had vada pav? (to a man)

examples.native: आम्ही गेल्या महिन्यात गोव्याला गेलो होतो.
examples.roman: āmhī gelyā mahinyāt govyālā gelo hoto.
examples.en: We went to Goa last month.

examples.native: मी पोहोचलो तेव्हा ते निघून गेले होते.
examples.roman: mī pohotslo tevhā te nighūn gele hote.
examples.en: When I got there, they'd already left. (man)

grammar.title: Past continuous: मी जेवत होतो — and what interrupted it
grammar.body:
For what you were **in the middle of**, use stem + **त** + the past of असणे (होतो, होते, होतास, होतीस, होता, होती, होतं, होतात, होते, होत्या):

मी झोप**त होतो** (m) / झोप**त होते** (f) 'I was sleeping'
तू काय कर**त होतास**? 'what were you doing?'
ते टीव्ही बघ**त होते** 'they were watching TV'

It always agrees with the **subject**, even with an object, and never takes -ने: **तो** जेवण करत **होता**, **ती** पुस्तक वाचत **होती**.

It sets the scene for something that happened, which comes in the plain past, often after **तेव्हा** 'then, at that point' or **आणि तेवढ्यात** 'and just then': मी अंघोळ करत होतो **तेव्हा** तुझा फोन आला.

**'Was going to':** stem + **णार होतो**: मी तुला फोन **करणार होतो** 'I was going to call you'; आम्ही निघणार होतो, पण पाऊस आला. Very handy for excuses.

**Don't confuse** it with **used to** (Unit 26): मी जिमला **जात होतो** 'I was going to the gym (at the time / on that day)', मी जिमला **जायचो** 'I used to go to the gym (regularly)'. In practice the -त होतो form is also used for a stretch of time in the past: तेव्हा मी पुण्यात राहत होतो 'back then I was living in Pune'.

examples.native: मी अंघोळ करत होतो, म्हणून फोन उचलला नाही.
examples.roman: mī aṅghoḷ karat hoto, mhaṇūn fon utsallā nāhī.
examples.en: I was in the shower, so I didn't pick up. (man)

examples.native: आम्ही गप्पा मारत होतो आणि तेवढ्यात पाऊस सुरू झाला.
examples.roman: āmhī gappā mārat hoto āṇi tevḍhyāt pāūs surū dzhālā.
examples.en: We were chatting and just then it started to rain.

examples.native: ती तेव्हा कुठे काम करत होती?
examples.roman: tī tevhā kuṭhe kām karat hotī?
examples.en: Where was she working back then?
I was just about to call you! (man)

examples.native: पाऊस पडत होता, म्हणून आम्ही घरीच थांबलो.
examples.roman: pāūs paḍat hotā, mhaṇūn āmhī gharīts thāmblo.
examples.en: It was raining, so we stayed at home.

grammar.title: For, since, ago: -पासून, -पूर्वी, -नी, -भर
grammar.body:
**-पासून** 'since / for (and still going on)'. Put the time word in the oblique, and — unlike English — keep the verb in the **present**:
मी दोन वर्षांपासून पुण्यात **राहतोय** 'I've been living in Pune for two years'
ती सोमवारपासून आजारी **आहे** 'she's been ill since Monday'
**कधीपासून?** 'since when? how long?' · **लहानपणापासून** 'since childhood' · सकाळपासून 'since the morning'

**-पूर्वी** 'ago' (colloquially also **-आधी**): दोन वर्षांपूर्वी 'two years ago', थोड्या वेळापूर्वी 'a little while ago', पाच मिनिटांपूर्वी.

**-नी / -नंतर** 'after (a gap of), later': **किती दिवसांनी!** 'after so long!', दोन तासांनी 'two hours later', लग्नानंतर 'after the wedding'.

**गेले / गेली + time** 'for the past…': गेले दोन महिने मी खूप बिझी आहे.

**-भर** 'the whole…': दिवसभर 'all day', रात्रभर 'all night', महिनाभर 'for a whole month'.

With a number, time words take the oblique plural: वर्ष → **वर्षांपासून**, दिवस → **दिवसांनी**, महिना → **महिन्यांपूर्वी**, तास → **तासांनी**, आठवडा → **आठवड्यांपूर्वी**.

**The trap:** ✗ मी दोन वर्षांपासून इथे राहिलोय. If it's still going on, it's the present: **राहतोय / राहतो**. And don't mix up **-पासून** (since, still going) with **-पूर्वी** (ago, done).

examples.native: मी तीन वर्षांपासून इथे काम करतोय.
examples.roman: mī tīn varṣānpāsūn ithe kām kartoy.
examples.en: I've been working here for three years. (man)
It's been years since we last met!

examples.native: गेले दोन महिने मी खूप बिझी आहे.
examples.roman: gele don mahine mī khūp bizī āhe.
examples.en: I've been really busy for the past two months.

dialogue.title: Is that you?
dialogue.setting: Sayali and Omkar were in college together. She's back in Pune on holiday and spots him at a café on JM Road.

lines.speaker: Sayali
lines.en: Omkar? Hey, it's you, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.native: सायली! मी तुला ओळखलंच नाही! किती वर्षांनी!
lines.roman: sāylī! mī tulā oḷakhlaṃts nāhī! kitī varṣānnī!
lines.en: Sayali! I didn't recognise you! It's been years!

lines.speaker: Sayali
lines.native: शेवटचं आपण कॉलेजच्या फेअरवेलला भेटलो होतो, ना?
lines.roman: shevaṭtsaṃ āpaṇ kôlejchyā feyarvellā bheṭlo hoto, nā?
lines.en: The last time we met was at the college farewell, right?

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.native: हो! बोल, काय म्हणतेस? सध्या काय चाललंय?
lines.roman: ho! bol, kāy mhaṇtes? sadhyā kāy tsāllaṃy?
lines.en: Yes! So tell me, how's it going? What are you up to these days?

lines.speaker: Sayali
lines.native: मी दोन वर्षांपासून बंगलोरला आहे, एका कंपनीत. आत्ता सुट्टीवर आलेय.
lines.roman: mī don varṣānpāsūn baṅglorlā āhe, ekā kampanīt. āttā suṭṭīvar āley.
lines.en: I've been in Bangalore for two years, at a company. I'm here on holiday.

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.native: भारी! आणि मध्यंतरी काय काय झालं? लग्न वगैरे?
lines.roman: bhārī! āṇi madhyantarī kāy kāy dzhālaṃ? lagna vagaire?
lines.en: Cool! And what else has happened? Married, or anything?

lines.speaker: Sayali
lines.native: काहीही! अजून नाही. तुझं काय? ऐकलं की तू नोकरी सोडलीस?
lines.roman: kāhīhī! adzūn nāhī. tudzhaṃ kāy? aiklaṃ kī tū nokrī soḍlīs?
lines.en: As if! Not yet. What about you? I heard you quit your job?

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.native: हो, सहा महिन्यांपूर्वी. आता मी सह्याद्रीत ट्रेक्स घेऊन जातो.
lines.roman: ho, sahā mahinyānpūrvī. ātā mī sahyādrīt ṭreks gheūn dzāto.
lines.en: Yes, six months ago. Now I lead treks in the Sahyadris.

lines.speaker: Sayali
lines.native: काय सांगतोस! मी कधीच ट्रेकला गेले नाही.
lines.roman: kāy sāṅgtos! mī kadhīts ṭreklā gele nāhī.
lines.en: No way! I've never been on a trek.

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.native: मग या रविवारी ये. आम्ही राजमाचीला जाणार आहोत.
lines.roman: mag yā ravivārī ye. āmhī rādzmāchīlā dzāṇār āhot.
lines.en: Then come this Sunday. We're going to Rajmachi.

lines.speaker: Sayali
lines.en: It'll be raining then, won't it?

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.native: हो, तीच तर मजा आहे! पावसात भिजायचं, धुक्यात भटकायचं…
lines.roman: ho, tīts tar madzā āhe! pāvsāt bhidzāytsaṃ, dhukyāt bhaṭkāytsaṃ…
lines.en: Yes, that's the whole fun of it! Getting soaked, wandering about in the mist…

lines.speaker: Sayali
lines.native: ठीक आहे, येते! पण मी पडले तर तुझी जबाबदारी!
lines.roman: ṭhīk āhe, yete! paṇ mī paḍle tar tujhī jabābdārī!
lines.en: OK, I'm in! But if I fall, it's on you!

culture: Friends catching up in Marathi skip 'how are you' and go straight to **काय म्हणतोस?** or **काय रे, कुठे गायब?** 'hey, where did you disappear to?'. Questions can be very direct — older relatives will ask about your job, your salary and your marriage plans within five minutes, and a vague **चाललंय** 'getting by' or **बघू** 'we'll see' is a perfectly acceptable answer. Weekend talk in Maharashtra is full of places: monsoon treks to the **Sahyadri** forts (सिंहगड, राजमाची, हरिश्चंद्रगड), quick trips to Lonavala or Mahabaleshwar, and the Konkan beaches (अलिबाग, गणपतीपुळे). **'पावसाळी ट्रेक'** is practically a Pune religion, and the forts carry a special pride because of **शिवाजी महाराज** — always with महाराज, never just 'Shivaji'. When someone shares big news, the natural reactions are **काय सांगतोस / सांगतेस!** 'you don't say!', **भारी!** and, for a pregnancy, a wedding or a new job, **अभिनंदन!** with a demand for पार्टी.

tip.title: काय म्हणतोस? — catching up with friends
tip.body:
- **काय म्हणतोस / म्हणतेस?** (friend) or **काय म्हणताय?** (polite) = 'how's it going?' — literally 'what do you say?'.
- **सध्या काय चाललंय?** 'what are you up to?', **काय नवीन?** 'what's new?'.
- Answers: **मजेत**, **विशेष काही नाही**, **चाललंय** 'getting by'.
- **किती दिवसांनी!** 'it's been ages!'

sentences.en: How's it going? All good? (to a woman)
How are things, Kaka? Everyone well?
When did we last meet?
What's been happening since I last saw you?

sentences.native: तू मला ओळखलंस का? मी नेहा, शाळेतली!
sentences.roman: tū malā oḷakhlaṃs kā? mī nehā, shāḷetlī!
sentences.en: Do you recognise me? I'm Neha, from school!
Nothing special, the usual.
What's going on at work these days?
It's been ages since you called!

sentences.native: आमची शेवटची भेट तुझ्या लग्नात झाली होती.
sentences.roman: āmchī shevaṭchī bheṭ tujhyā lagnāt dzhālī hotī.
sentences.en: The last time we met was at your wedding.

tip.title: गेलो, गेलोय, गेलो होतो
tip.body:
- **Plain past** गेलो = I went.
- **Perfect** = past + आहे, fused in speech: **आलोय**, **आलीय**, **आलेत**, **पाहिलाय** — the result matters now.
- **Past perfect** = past + **होतो / होती**: मी लोणावळ्याला **गेलो होतो** — Marathi's normal way to talk about a finished trip (you went and came back).
tip.pattern: मी गेलो · मी गेलोय · मी गेलो होतो

sentences.native: गेल्या वीकेंडला आम्ही अलिबागला गेलो होतो.
sentences.roman: gelyā vīkeṇḍlā āmhī alibāglā gelo hoto.
sentences.en: Last weekend we went to Alibag.
We wandered along the beach for ages.

sentences.native: तू त्या किल्ल्यावर कधी गेला होतास?
sentences.roman: tū tyā killyāvar kadhī gelā hotās?
sentences.en: When did you go up that fort? (to a man)
She's just got back from a trip.
I've taken loads of photos, look.

sentences.native: किल्ल्यावर पोहोचलो तेव्हा खूप धुकं होतं.
sentences.roman: killyāvar pohotslo tevhā khūp dhukaṃ hotaṃ.
sentences.en: When we reached the fort it was really misty.
I've seen this fort before.

sentences.native: ते सगळे आलेत, फक्त तू बाकी आहेस.
sentences.roman: te sagḷe ālet, phakta tū bākī āhes.
sentences.en: They've all arrived, it's just you we're waiting for.

sentences.native: आम्ही पावसात खूप भिजलो, पण धमाल आली!
sentences.roman: āmhī pāvsāt khūp bhidzlo, paṇ dhamāl ālī!
sentences.en: We got completely soaked in the rain, but it was a blast!

tip.title: कधी … का? — have you ever…?
tip.body:
- **Ever** = **कधी** + the perfect: तू कधी गोव्याला **गेलायस** का? · तुम्ही कधी ट्रेक **केलाय** का?
- **Never** = **कधीच** + the plain past negative: मी कधीच **गेलो नाही**.
- **Not yet** = **अजून** + negative: अजून नाही पाहिला.
- **For the first time** = **पहिल्यांदा(च)**.

sentences.native: तू कधी किल्ल्यावर ट्रेक केलायस का?
sentences.roman: tū kadhī killyāvar ṭrek kelāyas kā?
sentences.en: Have you ever done a fort trek? (to a man)
I've never been to Goa. (man)

sentences.native: तुम्ही कधी पावसात ट्रेक केलाय का?
sentences.roman: tumhī kadhī pāvsāt ṭrek kelāy kā?
sentences.en: Have you ever done a trek in the rain?

sentences.native: मी पहिल्यांदाच इतका मोठा किल्ला पाहतोय.
sentences.roman: mī pahilyāndāts itkā moṭhā killā pāhtoy.
sentences.en: It's the first time I've seen such a big fort. (man)
It was totally awesome!
Have you seen this film? (to a man)
No, I haven't seen it yet.
She's gone abroad for the first time.
He's never cooked in his life.

tip.title: -पासून, -पूर्वी, -नी — since, ago, after
tip.body:
- **-पासून** 'since / for' + **present** verb: मी दोन वर्षांपासून इथे **राहतो**.
- **-पूर्वी** 'ago': दोन वर्षांपूर्वी. **-नी** 'after': किती दिवसांनी!
- **-भर** 'the whole': दिवसभर, रात्रभर.
- Time words with a number go oblique plural: वर्षां-, महिन्यां-, दिवसां-, तासां-.

sentences.native: मी तीन महिन्यांपासून एक कोर्स करतोय.
sentences.roman: mī tīn mahinyānpāsūn ek kors kartoy.
sentences.en: I've been doing a course for three months. (man)

sentences.native: तू हा कोर्स कधी जॉईन केलास?
sentences.roman: tū hā kors kadhī jôīn kelās?
sentences.en: When did you join this course? (to a man)

sentences.native: मी दोन आठवड्यांपूर्वी नवीन नोकरी जॉईन केली.
sentences.roman: mī don āṭhavḍyānpūrvī navīn nokrī jôīn kelī.
sentences.en: I started a new job two weeks ago.
I haven't eaten anything since the morning.
I was at home all day yesterday. (man)
It's been quite a while since we met.
She's lived in Mumbai since she was little.

sentences.native: तो बराच वेळ तुझी वाट बघत होता.
sentences.roman: to barāts veḷ tujhī vāṭ baghat hotā.
sentences.en: He was waiting for you for quite a while.
We've been friends for five years.
I got here half an hour ago. (man)

tip.title: मी जेवत होतो — I was eating
tip.body:
- **stem + त + होतो / होते / होता / होती** = was …-ing, agreeing with the **subject** (no -ने): तो जेवण करत **होता**.
- What interrupted it comes in the plain past, often after **तेव्हा** or **आणि तेवढ्यात** 'and just then'.
- **stem + णार होतो** = was going to: मी फोन **करणार होतो**.

sentences.native: मी जिममध्ये व्यायाम करत होतो, म्हणून फोन उचलला नाही.
sentences.roman: mī jimmadhye vyāyām karat hoto, mhaṇūn fon utsallā nāhī.
sentences.en: I was working out at the gym, so I didn't pick up. (man)

sentences.native: मी स्टेशनवर ट्रेनची वाट बघत होतो आणि तेवढ्यात ती दिसली.
sentences.roman: mī sṭeshanvar ṭrenchī vāṭ baghat hoto āṇi tevḍhyāt tī dislī.
sentences.en: I was waiting for the train at the station and just then I spotted her. (man)
The train was really crowded.
What were you doing? (to a woman)

sentences.native: मी तुला मेसेज करणार होतो, पण विसरलो.
sentences.roman: mī tulā mesej karṇār hoto, paṇ visarlo.
sentences.en: I was going to text you, but I forgot. (man)

sentences.native: तुझ्यात खूप बदल झालाय! वजन कमी केलंस का?
sentences.roman: tujhyāt khūp badal dzhālāy! vadzan kamī kelaṃs kā?
sentences.en: You've changed so much! Have you lost weight?

sentences.native: मी रोज जिमला जायचो, पण आता वेळ नसतो.
sentences.roman: mī rodz jimlā dzāytso, paṇ ātā veḷ nasto.
sentences.en: I used to go to the gym every day, but now I don't have time. (man)

sentences.native: आम्ही जेवत होतो आणि तेवढ्यात बाबा आले.
sentences.roman: āmhī jevat hoto āṇi tevḍhyāt bābā āle.
sentences.en: We were eating and just then Dad came in.

sentences.native: पाऊस पडत होता आणि खूप गर्दी होती, म्हणून उशीर झाला.
sentences.roman: pāūs paḍat hotā āṇi khūp gardī hotī, mhaṇūn ushīr dzhālā.
sentences.en: It was raining and really crowded, so I got held up.

sentences.native: एक खुशखबर आहे — मला नोकरी मिळाली!
sentences.roman: ek khushkhabar āhe — malā nokrī miḷālī!
sentences.en: I've got some good news — I got the job!

sentences.native: तुला माहितेय का, नेहा गरोदर आहे!
sentences.roman: tulā māhitey kā, nehā garodar āhe!
sentences.en: Guess what — Neha's pregnant!
When's the baby due?

sentences.native: माझ्या बहिणीला गेल्या महिन्यात बाळ झालं.
sentences.roman: mājhyā bahiṇīlā gelyā mahinyāt bāḷ dzhālaṃ.
sentences.en: My sister had a baby last month.
I finally passed the exam! (man)

sentences.native: तो पहिल्यांदा नापास झाला, पण दुसऱ्यांदा पास झाला.
sentences.roman: to pahilyāndā nāpās dzhālā, paṇ dusryāndā pās dzhālā.
sentences.en: He failed the first time, but passed the second time.
Was it a boy or a girl?
The baby looks just like her.

sentences.native: त्यांनी नवीन घर घेतलंय आणि पुढच्या महिन्यात तिथे राहायला जाणार आहेत.
sentences.roman: tyānnī navīn ghar ghetlaṃy āṇi puḍhchyā mahinyāt tithe rāhāylā dzāṇār āhet.
sentences.en: They've bought a new house and are moving in next month.

sentences.native: आमच्या ग्रुपमधला अमित नोकरी सोडून परदेशात गेलाय.
sentences.roman: āmchyā grupmadhlā amit nokrī soḍūn pardeshāt gelāy.
sentences.en: Amit from our group has quit his job and moved abroad.
